Test Harvest Control Rule with a Butterfish-like stock

Sarah Gaichas

2026-08-19

Code modified from the SPASM.MSE vignettes

Vignettes found here

Starting point is this one https://lichengxue.github.io/SPASAM.MSE/Use-Actual-Stock-Assessment.html

And modifying to test the addition of the MAFMC risk policy and ABC HCR that I added to my own version of SPASAM.MSE::advice_fn()

Operating model setup

Basic information

This is all modified for butterfish

The 2022 butterfish RT models are posted online in the SASI portal here.

MT assessments are not posted (maybe someday?) but Chuck kindly sent the 2024 MT outputs when I requested them; and converted them to multi-wham, which I think made all the difference. A day or two was spent trying to make the RT model work but it kept blowing up because WHAM 2.0 is very different from WHAM 1.0

Global settings

input_hist <- buttermod$input #prepare_wham_input(gb_dat)
input      <- buttermod$input #prepare_wham_input(gb_dat)

n_stocks  <- 1L
n_regions <- 1L
n_ages    <- 5L # NAAmod2022$input$data$n_ages is 5
n_indices <- 6L # NAAmod2022$input$data$n_indices is 6
n_fleets  <- 1L # NAAmod2022$input$data$n_fleets is 1
n_seasons <- 1L

# butterfish RT assessment start and end data years NAAmod2022$years, updated for 2024 MT
year_start  <- 1989L
year_end    <- 2023L
MSE_years   <- 9L # 3 3yr assessment cycles

n_hist_years <- year_end - year_start + 1L
n_proj_years <- n_hist_years + MSE_years

base_years      <- year_start:year_end
assess_interval <- 3L

stopifnot(MSE_years %% assess_interval == 0L)

assess_years <- seq(
  tail(base_years, 1),
  year_end + MSE_years - assess_interval,
  by = assess_interval
)

# Historical period is fixed.
# Only years from first_free_year onward are allowed to vary.
first_free_year <- 37L # example has last-first year + assess interval

Scaffold

info <- SPASAM.MSE::generate_basic_info(
  n_stocks = n_stocks,
  n_regions = n_regions,
  n_indices = n_indices,
  n_fleets = n_fleets,
  n_seasons = n_seasons,
  base.years = year_start:year_end,
  n_feedback_years = MSE_years,
  n_ages = n_ages,
  catch_info = catch_info,
  index_info = index_info,
  user_waa = user_waa,
  user_maturity = user_maturity,
  fracyr_spawn = fracyr_spawn
)
## Using user-specified WAA array. WAA can be time-varying.
## 
##   --------------------
##   
##   IMPORTANT!!!!
##   
##   For the current version of WHAM, if WAA pointers are specified (i.e., WAA differs across fleets, indices, or stocks),
##   
##   they need to be updated *after* prepare_wham_input(). Otherwise, a global WAA will be applied to all components.
##           
##   --------------------
## 
## 
##   --------------------
##   IMPORTANT!!!!
##   
##   For the current version of WHAM:
##   
##   - If CV and effective sample size for **catch** vary over years,
##   or if some years have missing aggregate or age composition data for **catch**,
##   you must update these inputs *after* prepare_wham_input()
##   using the update_input_catch_info() function.
##   
##   - If CV and effective sample size for **indices** vary over years,
##   or if some years have missing aggregate or age composition data for **indices**,
##   you must update these inputs *after* prepare_wham_input()
##   using the update_input_index_info() function.
##   
##   Otherwise, WHAM will assume constant CV/sample size and complete data across all years.
##   --------------------
## 
basic_info     <- info$basic_info
catch_info_use <- info$catch_info
index_info_use <- info$index_info

catch_info_use$agg_catch[1:n_hist_years, ]     <- input$data$agg_catch
catch_info_use$catch_paa[, 1:n_hist_years, ]   <- input$data$catch_paa
index_info_use$agg_indices[1:n_hist_years, ]   <- input$data$agg_indices
index_info_use$index_paa[, 1:n_hist_years, ]   <- input$data$index_paa
# index_info_use_hist$use_indices[1:n_hist_years, ]   <- input$data$use_indices
# index_info_use_hist$use_index_paa[1:n_hist_years, ] <- input$data$use_index_paa

# OM$input$data$selblock_pointer_fleets has selectivity years for fishery, added

M <- list(
  model = "constant",
  initial_means = array(
    c(1.278, 1.278, 1.278, 1.278, 1.278),
    dim = c(n_stocks, n_regions, n_ages)
  )
)

sigma_vals <- array(0, dim = c(n_stocks, n_regions, n_ages))
sigma_vals[, , 1] <- exp(OM$parList$log_NAA_sigma[, , 1])
sigma_vals[, , 2:n_ages] <- exp(OM$parList$log_NAA_sigma[, , 2:n_ages])

recruit_pars_use <- exp(as.numeric(OM$parList$mean_rec_pars[1, ]))

NAA_re <- list(
  N1_model      = rep("age-specific-fe", n_stocks),
  sigma         = rep("rec+1", n_stocks),
  cor           = rep("iid", n_stocks),
  recruit_model = 2,
  recruit_pars  = list(recruit_pars_use),
  sigma_vals    = sigma_vals
)

## --Input Complete--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## WHAM version 2.0.0 and forward: 
## 1) makes major changes to the structure of some data, parameters, and reported objects.
## 2) decouples random effects for recruitment and random effects for older ages by default. To obtain results from previous versions set NAA_re$decouple_recruitment = FALSE.
## 3) does not bias correct any log-normal process or observation errors. To configure these, set basic_info$bias_correct_process = TRUE and/or basic_info$bias_correct_observation = TRUE.
## -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## input$data$spawn_regions will be defined from input$data$NAA_where for age 1.
## --Catch------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ 
## catch_info$waa_pointer_fleets was not provided, so the first waa matrix will be used for all fleets. 
## Selectivity blocks for each fleet:
## Fleet 1: 1, 2
## 
## -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 
## --Indices----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Selectivity blocks for each index:
## index_1: 3
## index_2: 4
## index_3: 5
## index_4: 6
## index_5: 7
## index_6: 8
## 
## -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 
## --NAA--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 
##  Same NAA_re$sigma being used for all stocks (rec+1).
## -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 
## --Selectivity------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## (Mean) selectivity block models are:
## Block 1: age-specific
## Block 2: age-specific
## Block 3: age-specific
## Block 4: age-specific
## Block 5: age-specific
## Block 6: age-specific
## Block 7: age-specific
## Block 8: age-specific
## 
## Random effects options for each selectivity block are:
## Block 1: none
## Block 2: none
## Block 3: none
## Block 4: none
## Block 5: none
## Block 6: none
## Block 7: none
## Block 8: none
## 
## -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 
## --OSA obs----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Selectivity block 6 has parameters for ages 1 fixed at 0 and is used by index 4
##  in years 1989, 1990, 1991, 1992, 1993, 1994, 1995, 1996, 1997, 1998, 1999, 2000, 2001, 2002, 2003, 2004, 2005, 2006, 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027, 2028, 2029, 2030, 2031, 2032.
## Observations at these ages will be omitted and remaining observations will be rescaled.
## 
## -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 
## --Reference points-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## For annual SPR-based reference points, corresponding annual conditionally expected recruitments are used. 
## -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
waa_info <- info$par_inputs$user_waa
om_input_P <- SPASAM.MSE::update_waa(om_input_P, waa_info = waa_info)

om_input_P$par$index_paa_pars <- OM$parList$index_paa_pars #<- matrix(0, basic_info$n_indices, 3) #these were not in the old OM
om_input_P$par$sel_repars     <- OM$parList$sel_repars

for (i in 1:n_regions) {
  om_input_P$par$log_N1[i, i, ] <- log(OM$rep$N1)[i, i, ] #log(OM$rep$NAA[i, 1])  #for old model
}

om_input_P$data$agg_index_sigma[1:n_hist_years, ] <- input_hist$data$agg_index_sigma
om_input_P$data$use_indices[1:n_hist_years, ]     <- input_hist$data$use_indices
om_input_P$data$use_index_paa[1:n_hist_years, ]   <- input_hist$data$use_index_paa

for (iy in (n_hist_years + 1L):n_proj_years) {

Now adding back indices with years to use, works now

loc_zeros_agg <- lapply(seq_len(ncol(input_hist$data$use_indices)), function(j) {
  which(input_hist$data$use_indices[, j] == 0)
})

loc_zeros_paa <- lapply(seq_len(ncol(input_hist$data$use_index_paa)), function(j) {
  which(input_hist$data$use_index_paa[, j] == 0)
})

max_agg <- max(sapply(loc_zeros_agg, length))
max_paa <- max(sapply(loc_zeros_paa, length))

remove_agg_years1 <- if (max_agg > 0) {
  out <- matrix(NA_integer_, nrow = max_agg, ncol = length(loc_zeros_agg))
  for (j in seq_along(loc_zeros_agg)) {
    if (length(loc_zeros_agg[[j]])) {
      out[seq_along(loc_zeros_agg[[j]]), j] <- loc_zeros_agg[[j]]
    }
  }
  out
} else NULL

remove_paa_years1 <- if (max_paa > 0) {
  out <- matrix(NA_integer_, nrow = max_paa, ncol = length(loc_zeros_paa))
  for (j in seq_along(loc_zeros_paa)) {
    if (length(loc_zeros_paa[[j]])) {
      out[seq_along(loc_zeros_paa[[j]]), j] <- loc_zeros_paa[[j]]
    }
  }
  out
} else NULL

om_input_P <- SPASAM.MSE::update_input_index_info(
  om_input_P,
  agg_index_sigma = om_input_P$data$agg_index_sigma,
  index_Neff      = om_input_P$data$index_Neff,
  remove_agg = TRUE,
  remove_agg_pointer = 1:6,
  remove_agg_years = remove_agg_years1,
  remove_paa = TRUE,
  remove_paa_pointer = 1:6,
  remove_paa_years = remove_paa_years1
)

}

## 
## Now conducting stock assessment for year 2023
## Using user-specified WAA array. WAA can be time-varying.
## 
##   --------------------
##   
##   IMPORTANT!!!!
##   
##   For the current version of WHAM, if WAA pointers are specified (i.e., WAA differs across fleets, indices, or stocks),
##   
##   they need to be updated *after* prepare_wham_input(). Otherwise, a global WAA will be applied to all components.
##           
##   --------------------
## 
## 
##   --------------------
##   IMPORTANT!!!!
##   
##   For the current version of WHAM:
##   
##   - If CV and effective sample size for **catch** vary over years,
##   or if some years have missing aggregate or age composition data for **catch**,
##   you must update these inputs *after* prepare_wham_input()
##   using the update_input_catch_info() function.
##   
##   - If CV and effective sample size for **indices** vary over years,
##   or if some years have missing aggregate or age composition data for **indices**,
##   you must update these inputs *after* prepare_wham_input()
##   using the update_input_index_info() function.
##   
##   Otherwise, WHAM will assume constant CV/sample size and complete data across all years.
##   --------------------
## 
## 
## --Creating input---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## basic_info done
## catch done
## indices done
## WAA done
## NAA done
## q done
## selectivity done
## age_comp done
## F done
## M done
## move done
## osa_obs done
## --Input Complete--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## WHAM version 2.0.0 and forward: 
## 1) makes major changes to the structure of some data, parameters, and reported objects.
## 2) decouples random effects for recruitment and random effects for older ages by default. To obtain results from previous versions set NAA_re$decouple_recruitment = FALSE.
## 3) does not bias correct any log-normal process or observation errors. To configure these, set basic_info$bias_correct_process = TRUE and/or basic_info$bias_correct_observation = TRUE.
## -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## input$data$spawn_regions will be defined from input$data$NAA_where for age 1.
## --Catch------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ 
## catch_info$waa_pointer_fleets was not provided, so the first waa matrix will be used for all fleets. 
## Selectivity blocks for each fleet:
## Fleet 1: 1
## 
## -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 
## --Indices----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Selectivity blocks for each index:
## index_1: 2
## index_2: 3
## index_3: 4
## index_4: 5
## index_5: 6
## index_6: 7
## 
## -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 
## --NAA--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 
##  Same NAA_re$sigma being used for all stocks (rec).
## -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 
## --Selectivity------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## (Mean) selectivity block models are:
## Block 1: age-specific
## Block 2: age-specific
## Block 3: age-specific
## Block 4: age-specific
## Block 5: age-specific
## Block 6: age-specific
## Block 7: age-specific
## Block 8: age-specific
## 
## Age-specific mean model set for selectivity block 3, but there are no observations > 0 for some ages corresponding to parameters specified to be estimated so they have been fixed at 0.
